memberdef.name: spectralDerivative

briefdescription.para: Derivative of an isotropic function of a symmetric tensor (Daleckii-Krein formula).

detaileddescription.para:
eigenvalues
Eigenvalues $ \lambda_a $ of the tensor.
eigenvectors
Its eigenvectors, by column.
dividedDifference
$ \theta(\lambda_a, \lambda_b) $: $ (f(\lambda_a) - f(\lambda_b)) / (\lambda_a - \lambda_b) $, and $ f'(\lambda_a) $ for equal arguments.
$ \partial f(\boldsymbol{C})_{ij}/\partial C_{IJ} = \sum_{a,b} \theta(\lambda_a, \lambda_b)\, Q_{ia} Q_{jb} Q_{Ia} Q_{Jb} $, for a symmetric increment of $ \boldsymbol{C} $.
The divided difference is continuous where eigenvalues coincide, so the formula holds for repeated eigenvalues as well, whatever eigenvectors the decomposition picks within the eigenspace.

briefdescription.para: Decorator presenting a small-strain gradient-enhanced material as a finite-strain one, in the frame of the polar rotation.

detaileddescription.para:
BaseMaterialType
A concrete class derived from Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic<n>; the wrapper has the same n nonlocal variables.
The deformation gradient is decomposed into the polar rotation and the right stretch, $ \boldsymbol{F} = \boldsymbol{R}\,\boldsymbol{U} $, $ \boldsymbol{U} = \boldsymbol{C}^{1/2} $, $ \boldsymbol{C} = \boldsymbol{F}^T\boldsymbol{F} $. The wrapped material lives in the frame that rotates with $ \boldsymbol{R} $ (the frame of the material fibres; Green-Naghdi): it is driven by the increment of the logarithmic (Hencky) strain \[ \Delta\hat{\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}} = \ln\boldsymbol{U}^{(n+1)} - \ln\boldsymbol{U}^{(n)}, \qquad \ln\boldsymbol{U} = \tfrac12\ln\boldsymbol{C}, \] and its stress is read as the rotated Kirchhoff stress, which is rotated out, \[ \boldsymbol{\tau} = \boldsymbol{R}\,\hat{\boldsymbol{\tau}}\,\boldsymbol{R}^T . \]

Why this frame. A superposed rigid rotation changes $ \boldsymbol{R} $ and leaves $ \boldsymbol{U} $ and hence everything the wrapped material sees unchanged, so the Kirchhoff stress rotates exactly, whatever the wrapped material does with its own state. That is what Marmot::Materials::GradientEnhancedHughesWingetWrapper cannot offer a material that recomputes its stress from total strains (GM7 does: its stress is the homogenized microplane stress of its stored strains, and the stress it is handed is overwritten); it rotates the stress it hands over, which such a material discards. Tensor-valued internal variables of the wrapped material (GM7's microplane state, its stored strains) live in the rotating frame too, so they are objective as well.

Why the logarithmic strain. It sums to a total strain, $ \sum\Delta\hat{\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}} = \ln\boldsymbol{U} $, independent of the path, so a material that accumulates its strain stores the Hencky strain; and under a pure stretch $ \lambda $ it hands the material $ \ln\lambda = (\lambda-1) + O((\lambda- 1)^2) $, i.e. the wrapped model is recovered up to second order in the strain. The rotated Kirchhoff stress is the stress work-conjugate to $ \ln\boldsymbol{U} $ for an isotropic response, so the elastic and dissipated energies the wrapped material reports are densities per unit reference volume and are passed through unchanged.

The nonlocal fields are handed over as they are (see GradientEnhancedHypoElasticWrapper): they are referred to the rotating frame as well for GM7, the nonlocal strain is the nonlocal counterpart of $ \hat{\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}} $ and their balance is written in the reference configuration, so they are invariant under a superposed rigid rotation.

entry.para: Tangent. Consistent and analytic: \[ \frac{\partial\tau_{ij}}{\partial F_{kL}} = \frac{\partial R_{ia}}{\partial F_{kL}}\,\hat\tau_{ab}\,R_{jb} + R_{ia}\,\hat\tau_{ab}\, \frac{\partial R_{jb}}{\partial F_{kL}} + R_{ia}R_{jb}\,\mathbb{C}_{abcd}\, \frac{\partial(\ln U)_{cd}}{\partial F_{kL}}, \qquad \frac{\partial\boldsymbol{R}}{\partial F_{kL}} = \Bigl(\frac{\partial\boldsymbol{F}}{\partial F_{kL}} - \boldsymbol{R}\,\frac{\partial\boldsymbol{U}}{\partial F_{kL}}\Bigr)\boldsymbol{U}^{-1}, \] with $ \mathbb{C} $ the algorithmic tangent of the wrapped material and the derivatives of the isotropic tensor functions $ \ln\boldsymbol{U} = \tfrac12\ln\boldsymbol{C} $ and $ \boldsymbol{U} = \boldsymbol{C}^{1/2} $ from the spectral decomposition of $ \boldsymbol{C} $ (spectralDerivative()). It is exact for any wrapped material whose stress does not depend on the stress it is handed (GM7), and for an incremental one too, since the stress it is handed is the rotated stress of the last call, which does not depend on $ \boldsymbol{F} $. The explicit path, computeStressExplicit(), skips it.

What it refuses. $ \boldsymbol{C} = \boldsymbol{F}^T\boldsymbol{F} $ is the same for $ \boldsymbol{F} $ and for its mirror image, so the strain does not show that a material point is turned inside out ( $ \det\boldsymbol{F} < 0 $; $ \boldsymbol{F} = -\boldsymbol{1} $ would be a point without strain or stress, with a reflection for $ \boldsymbol{R} $). A deformation gradient without a positive determinant is refused (std::invalid_argument).

The state of the wrapper: $ \ln\boldsymbol{U} $ and $ \hat{\boldsymbol{\tau}} $ of the last call (both in Voigt notation, the strain with engineering shear), the nonlocal fields of the last call, and the state of the wrapped material. A zero state is the undeformed, stress-free one, so no initialization beyond the wrapped material's is needed.
